noveltyJustification: The finding is fully new: no prior iteration examined the Python fallback's typed-mark handling or the bridge-normalization path.
keyQuestions: Which changes in the window introduced a bug, a dead reference or a broken cross-link?
ruledOut: A gate that reads rows by the wrong id: the gate runs before the rename, so bridge ids are correct there
A fan-out stop that records a live lineage as stopped: the confirmation loop re-reads the process table
A band budget that carries upward: carry is applied only to the next band
A pass-evidence off-by-one on a same-millisecond commit: the window bounds are correct for sequential commits
An incomplete cli-orca removal: every runtime mirror and live tree is clean

label: The typed mark is dropped when a run row is normalized onto an existing owner row: _apply_deep_loop_offer_gate sets rec[typed]=True at skill_advisor.py:4624 and the comment at 4562 says the rename carries it, but normalize_command_bridge_recommendations copies only confidence, uncertainty, passes_threshold, _kind_priority and _explicit_skill_match from the top row (3338-3362), so the field is lost when the owner row exists; no in-repo consumer reads it.
Frontier admission checks relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, node cap, budget and cycle in the notes' order, and each prune records its own reason.
The band budget carries an unused allotment only when the band has no open node left, so it rolls down and never up.
Pass evidence flags future_stamp, no_reads_no_findings and batched_commit exactly as the notes describe, leaving an undecidable pass at null.
The blocked-stop streak extends only on the same blocker-set key and stops at the configured threshold.
The cli-orca removal is complete across .opencode, .claude, .codex, .pi, .vibe and .dsh; only spec scratch artifacts mention it.
